nodes.content: Develop robotic active perception that resolves grasp-relevant occlusions while accounting for uncertain object motion induced by sensing actions.
requirements: Reduce failed grasps by 20% relative to a fixed-view baseline under matched action budgets.
Maintain object-damage rates below 1% across previously unseen object dynamics and occlusion patterns.

nodes.content: Use risk-constrained belief-space MPC to select occlusion-clearing views or probes using action-conditioned motion ensembles and a 0.5% damage-risk cap.
How can action-conditioned motion ensembles calibrate damage-risk estimates for unseen objects while selecting probes that reveal occluded grasp surfaces?
Contact-stratified conformal calibration will keep unseen-object damage below 1% while ensemble-guided probes cut occluded-grasp failures ≥20% versus budget-matched fixed views.
Run OccluMotion-2000 on held-out dynamics and occlusions, comparing conformally calibrated probes against budget-matched fixed views for damage and grasp-failure rates.
On OccluMotion-2000, contact-calibrated probes cut held-out grasp failures from 20% to 15% versus budget-matched fixed views; damage was 0.4%.
Advance contact-calibrated probing to the next validation stage; held-out grasp failures fell 25% while damage remained 0.4%.
After advancement, test 500 novel-dynamics grasps under unseen occlusions against budget-matched fixed views; verify ≥20% fewer failures and <1% damage.
Randomize 500 novel-dynamics grasps across unseen occlusions between contact-calibrated probing and fixed-view control, matching budgets and recording failures and damage.
OccluMotion-500 validation bundle containing randomized arm assignments, matched-budget action traces, held-out dynamics labels, grasp outcomes, and object-damage annotations.
Audit OccluMotion-500 labels and matched budgets; estimate stratified failure-reduction and damage confidence intervals against 20% and 1% thresholds.
On held-out OccluMotion-500, budget-matched failures fell from 50/250 (20%) to 36/250 (14.4%) with probing; probe damage was 1/250 (0.4%).
Low-force microprobe updates will limit unseen-material damage-risk underestimation to ≤0.5 percentage points and cut grasp failures ≥20% versus fixed views.
Test MaterialShift-2000: 1,000 unseen-material grasps per arm; compare low-force microprobe-updated damage-risk calibration and grasp failures against budget-matched fixed views.
On MaterialShift-2000, microprobes predicted 0.4% damage but observed 1.4% (14/1,000); grasp failures fell only from 20% to 17%.
Can material-shift gating replace risky microprobes with noncontact views while retaining ≥20% grasp-failure reduction and <1% damage?
Train vision-based material-shift gating to replace flagged microprobes with noncontact views; compare budget-matched grasp failures and damage on held-out materials.
Train a vision-embedding shift detector on separate development materials, routing flagged objects to noncontact camera views instead of microprobes.
MaterialGate-v1 contains a trained vision-embedding shift detector and routing policy that substitutes noncontact views for flagged microprobes.
Combine MaterialGate-v1 with action-conditioned belief-space planning: select noncontact views for material shifts and calibrated probes otherwise.
Where should MaterialGate-v1 set its shift threshold to avoid damaging missed detections without suppressing informative probes?
Setting MaterialGate-v1's threshold for ≥95% damage-prone-material recall keeps damage <1% and reduces grasp failures ≥20% versus budget-matched fixed views.
Set MaterialGate-v1's threshold for ≥95% development recall; test unseen MaterialShift-2kB recall, damage, and budget-matched failures versus fixed views.
On MaterialShift-2kB, MaterialGate-v1 recalled 96% of damage-prone materials; failures fell from 20% to 15.4%, with 0.6% damage.
Advance MaterialGate-v1 and calibrated probing to integration trials: separately, failures fell 23% and 28%, with 0.6% and 0.4% damage.
After advancement, tune MaterialGate-v1 thresholds for ≥95% damage-prone recall; validate integrated failure, damage, and probe rates on unseen materials.
Sweep MaterialGate-v1 thresholds on development materials, logging damage-prone recall and retained probe rate; freeze the ≥95%-recall setting.
MaterialGate-v1 threshold card freezes a 0.37 shift-score cutoff achieving ≥95% development recall, with retained-probe curves and routing rules.
Audit OccluMotion-500 outcomes and budgets; prospectively assess frozen 0.37 gate on unseen materials for failures, damage, and probe retention.
On MaterialShift-3k, ungated ensemble-MPC (0.5% cap) caused 1.3% damage; MaterialGate-v1 MPC caused 0.6%, with 23% fewer failures than fixed views.
Stress-test integrated MaterialGate-v1 MPC's frozen 0.37 cutoff on unseen-material, unseen-occlusion OccluDyn-1000; measure probe retention, damage, and budget-matched failures.
On OccluDyn-1000, frozen-gate MPC caused 1.2% damage (6/500); failures fell from 20% to 17% versus budget-matched fixed views.
Defer frozen-gate MPC deployment: MaterialShift-3k passed, but OccluDyn-1000 exceeded the damage limit and achieved only 15% fewer failures.
After deferral, calibrate occlusion-conditioned gate thresholds for ≥95% damage-prone recall; retest damage, probe retention, and failures on unseen dynamics.
Starting from MaterialGate-v1's 0.37 cutoff, tune occlusion-stratified thresholds on OccluGate-Dev for ≥95% damage-prone recall and maximal probe retention.
MaterialGate-v2 threshold card replaces uniform 0.37 with mild/moderate/severe-occlusion cutoffs of 0.37/0.30/0.23, plus probe-routing and development-recall tables.
Test MaterialGate-v2’s cutoffs with integrated MPC on novel-dynamics, unseen-occlusion OccluDyn-2k versus budget-matched fixed views; measure failures, damage, probe retention.
On OccluDyn-2k, MaterialGate-v2 MPC cut failures from 20% to 17% versus budget-matched fixed views; damage was 0.7%.
Defer deployment: v2 lowers OccluDyn damage from 1.2% to 0.7% but leaves failure reduction at 15%, unlike MaterialShift’s 23%.
Augment MaterialGate-v2 MPC with grasp-surface visibility rewards and motion-robust camera views, retaining probes only when calibrated safe.
Can grasp-surface visibility rewards recover OccluDyn’s missing failure reduction without raising damage above 1% under motion uncertainty?
Adding motion-robust grasp-surface visibility rewards to MaterialGate-v2 MPC will reduce OccluDyn failures to ≤16%, with damage <1%.
Using MaterialGate-v1’s detector, compare motion-robust visibility-rewarded v2 MPC against standard v2 and budget-matched fixed views on OccluDyn-3k: failures, damage.
On OccluDyn-3k, visibility-rewarded MPC had 15.6% failures versus 17% standard v2 and 20% budget-matched fixed views; damage was 0.6%.
Advance visibility-rewarded MaterialGate-v2 MPC to validation: OccluDyn-3k met failure-reduction and damage targets, unlike standard v2.
After advancement, test visibility-rewarded MPC on unseen-dynamics OccluDyn-4k against budget-matched fixed views; verify ≥20% fewer failures and <1% damage.
Deploy MaterialGate-v1’s detector within visibility-rewarded v2 MPC for randomized OccluDyn-4k trials, logging motion, budgets, failures, and damage.
OccluDyn-4k trial bundle contains randomized assignments, matched-budget action logs, object-motion trajectories, grasp outcomes, and damage annotations.
Audit OccluDyn-4k randomization and budgets; compare visibility-rewarded MPC against fixed views using failure-reduction and damage confidence bounds.
On OccluDyn-4k, visibility-rewarded MPC cut failures from 400/2,000 (20%) to 340/2,000 (17%), only 15%; damage was 0.7%.
Defer deployment: visibility-rewarded MPC achieved 22% fewer failures on OccluDyn-3k but only 15% on validation OccluDyn-4k.
Do action-induced rotations under severe occlusion make predicted grasp-surface visibility unreliable on OccluDyn-4k?
For severely occluded OccluDyn-4k objects, sensing-induced rotations >15° will double grasp-surface visibility-fraction MAE versus rotations ≤5°.
For deferred-deployment requalification, rerun MaterialGate-v1 routing on OccluDyn-4k logs; compare severe-occlusion visibility MAE for ≤5°/>15° rotations.
On severe-occlusion OccluDyn-4k, visibility-fraction MAE reached 0.24 after >15° rotations versus 0.10 after ≤5°, undermining motion-robust views.
Defer deployment; pursue rotation-aware visibility calibration because early gains did not generalize, and severe-occlusion rotations raised visibility MAE to 0.24.
